# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

## PR Description

Fixes #1257 (follow-up to gh-1244 / PR #1245 — reuses its established pattern verbatim, no second convention).

## Root Cause

Same flake class as gh-1244: five residual synchronization points pinned an exact transient bullet count on the raw stream (`waitForText('•••••')`). Under CI timing the PTY paints past the checkpoint before the 50 ms poll evaluates, and on the raw wire the focused secret row wraps the cursor cell in inverse-video escapes (`_secretValueSegmentRow` / `_cursorInputRow` in `lib/src/cli/tui_prompt.dart`), so N consecutive `•` need never exist in the stream at all. The feature was correct; the anchors were wrong. No production code changes.

## Fix (test-only, 2 files)

- `test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart`
  - RT1 (2 sites): the `waitForText('•••••')` checkpoints before each grant Enter replaced with the PR #1245 `typeSecret` property anchor (copied 1:1: `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + one re-anchor if `maskedValueRow` is null + race-free raw-transcript plaintext scan + frame-closed row bullet count == typed length).
  - RT4 (multiline paste): anchored on the painted screen's full first-segment run (`'•' * 19`); the masking property asserts the multiline shape `tui_prompt` actually renders — one bullet per pasted char, ONE FRAME ROW PER LINE (`[19, 6, 17]` over all `│`-closed masked rows) — plus the raw-transcript plaintext scan (`maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows; a single-row count can never see all 44 bullets).
  - RT5 (over-wide paste): `_wrapBodyLine` TRIMS an over-wide value row to the frame budget, so the full 200-bullet mask can never paint; anchored on a 40-bullet leading run (trimmed run is 75 cells at the 80-col PTY), asserting the frame-closed value row is all bullets (count >= 40, no `kk` anywhere on the anchored screen) + raw-transcript scan.
- `test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart`
  - The one `waitForText('•••••')` site converted to the same property anchor (`waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + `maskedValueRow` re-anchor + plaintext scans on the anchored screen); the pre-existing post-Enter raw checks unchanged.

AC1 verified statically: `grep -rn "waitForText('•••••')" test/` → no code hits remain (one doc-comment mention in the converted file explains the replaced anti-pattern).

## Relationship to PR #1284 (base secret_sheet_test quarantine)

#1284 quarantined `secret_sheet_test.dart` for the PTY **boot-timeout** signature (freeze-ledger 1st hit at secret_sheet_test.dart:194) — a different failure mode from this ticket's bullet-anchor class (same PTY integration family, different sig). This PR does not touch that file, the quarantine entry, or `pty_harness.dart` (hot zone — no harness changes were needed; `maskedValueRow` already on main covers all sites). Whether the #1284 quarantine can lift is independent of this lane.

## Test Coverage / Gate disclosure

- Local targeted gate `dart test test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart --tags integration` attempted ONCE on the fleet Mac box and **SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137)** — the known live-LLM-loop condition; no output faked, not retried. The hermetic `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` guard rules were verified by inspection instead (every `waitForScreen` captures its result; no unanchored screen reads in danger windows).
- **PR CI is the real gate**: the pty/nightly legs run both files; AC2 (repeated green runs of the PTY leg) is CI-side by construction — the anchors synchronize on stable painted-screen properties, so a raced checkpoint can no longer be missed.
- No timeouts raised beyond the 1245 precedent (30 s screen waits), no sleeps added.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary

  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →

  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —

  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold

blocks.text:
The typeSecret copy matches the precedent nearly verbatim. Now let me evaluate the actual review points.

Key areas to scrutinize:

1. **password_prompt_pty_test.dart**: the `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` for `secret = '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` (15 chars). Does the password prompt's masked row close with `│`? The test doesn't call maskedValueRow for the count assertion — it only uses it as a re-anchor check. Fine.

   However: one subtle issue — in the password prompt test, is the masked row frame-closed with `│`? Doesn't matter, it's only used for re-anchor.

2. **Race concern in RT4's multiline rows assertion**: `maskedRows` filters ALL rows that contain '•' and end with '│'. The first-segment run is 19 bullets; anchor is `'•' * 19`. Fine. But does any other frame row potentially contain bullets? E.g., the reason row or name row wouldn't contain bullets. OK.

   One issue: RT4 asserts exact list `[19, 6, 17]`. Is this over-pinning a rendering shape that could legitimately change? It's a masking property — pinned intentionally. Fine.

3. **RT5 anchor `'•' * 40`**: comment says the trimmed run is 75 cells at 80-col PTY. Wait — the anchor on a 40-bullet run: `waitForScreen` checks `screenText.contains('•' * 40)`. Could 40 consecutive bullets appear across a WRAPPED row? `expectFrameIntact` requires rows don't wrap. Also the bullet run could exist partially... it's monotone, fine.

   Hmm, one subtle problem in RT5: `maskedValueRow(screen)` gets the FIRST frame-closed bullet row. But the row at the anchor time might be an intermediate frame — e.g., bracketed paste updates arrive in chunks? `sendText` writes the entire paste at once, so one buffer update. The row bullets: 200 chars trimmed to 75 cells. Could the first frame show fewer than 75 bullets and the row is already frame-closed? The assertion is >= 40, robust to that. Good.

4. **RT4 raw-output check**: `harness.rawOutput.contains(pasted)` — the pasted contains newlines; raw output would carry `\r\n`? Bracketed paste with raw mode... the CLI's input handling wouldn't echo. The check that no `\r` survives is done on the transcript. If the terminal converts LF to CRLF in echo... not echoed anyway. Pre-existing pattern though (typeSecret does the same with `secret`). Fine.

5. **The RT4 maskedRows potential flake**: `.where((l) => l.contains('•') && l.trimRight().endsWith('│'))` — if the anchored frame catches a row before its closing border, that row is excluded from maskedRows, causing [19,6] vs [19,6,17] failure. But typeSecret precedent re-anchors once on null; RT4 does NOT re-anchor. The anchor `'•' * 19` exists only once the pasted frame painted... but frame rows could paint one at a time. The waitForScreen returns the first frame containing 19 bullets — that frame may not yet have all three rows closed. Hmm, actually if 19 bullets of row 1 are painted, rows below paint later. The bullet rows are painted presumably in one repaint (single buffer update), but the frame-closing border repaint may lag (as noted in typeSecret's re-anchor comment). If the value rows are painted before the frame's closing border, the `.endsWith('│')` filter would drop rows → maskedRows mismatch → flake. The typeSecret precedent explicitly tolerates "the anchored frame can still predate the value row's closing border by one repaint; re-anchor once". RT4 and RT5 don't do the re-anchor. RT5 does check via maskedValueRow and throws StateError if null (which would be a hard failure, not a re-anchor). Actually RT5: `final row = maskedValueRow(screen); if (row == null) throw StateError(...)` — same as typeSecret's post-re-anchor behavior. But RT4 does no re-anchor at all before filtering.

   Is this a real flake risk? The PR claims the re-anchor concern applies where relevant. In RT4, the anchor is 19 bullets on the screen; when that paints, the frame is being drawn — each row individually ends with `│`. Does the masked value row end with `│` immediately when painted? The border column is painted as part of the frame; tui_prompt paints the whole frame per repaint presumably. In a single repaint, all rows close. The race window is between the 19-bullet row painting and the frame border painting — if they're separate repaint passes. typeSecret's re-anchor was added exactly because of this observed race (gh-1244 review thread). RT4/RT5 lack it. But waitForScreen returns at the first frame containing '•'*19; the frame content could be partially painted if dart_tui diffs and emits row by row... Actually the xterm emulator assembles the final screen; the "screen" at poll time is the current emulator state which may show a half-painted frame. Since waitForScreen polls every 50ms, and dart_tui emits whole frames quickly, the probability of catching a torn frame is low but nonzero — that's exactly why the re-anchor exists in the pattern this PR claims to copy "1:1". This is at most a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT consistency point: RT4 and RT5 skip the re-anchor that the copied pattern includes.

   Hmm, but the PR description says "the `maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows". It deliberately deviates. The risk: on a loaded CI runner, if the anchored frame predates a border, `maskedRows` would be `[19]` or `[19, 6]` etc. → test fails → new flake, the very thing this PR fixes. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (consistency with the established pattern; real flake-class risk), or SUGGESTION. Given the repo treats flake recurrence seriously, I'd say IMPORTANT.

6. **RT5 `screen.contains('kk')` check**: checks no two consecutive 'k' anywhere on the screen. Fine. But note: 'k' could appear in other legit screen text? Contains 'kk' — words with double-k unlikely. Fine.

7. **password test**: removed `expect(harness.screenText.contains(secret), isFalse)` replaced with anchored screen check. Slightly weaker (no longer checks the LIVE screen at that moment), but rawOutput covers everything and the anchored screen is asserted. Acceptable — documented. Also note reg-test: `waitForScreen` result captured — yes, `var screen = ...`. RT1 typeSecret captures. RT4/RT5 capture. Good.

8. **RT1 second site** (`second-secret`, 13 chars): `typeSecret` asserts row bullet count == 13. The history tool row `• request_secret · …` contains a single bullet, not frame-closed — filtered. But wait: the first secret was 's3cr3t-TOKEN-42' (15 chars). When typing the second secret, could the anchored screen still contain the FIRST sheet's row with 15 bullets and the second's with 13? The sheet fully replaced — first row gone (RT1 asserts no '•••' before). maskedValueRow takes the FIRST matching row; if a ghost of the old row lingered, count would be 15 ≠ 13 → fail loudly. That's a correct assertion.

9. **Timeout raise**: from 10s to 30s — consistent with 1245 precedent. Fine.

10. **RT4 maskedRows includes rows beyond the sheet?** The value field's masked rows end with '│'. Any other row on screen containing '•' and ending with '│'? The secret sheet frame's other rows (name, reason) don't contain bullets. OK. But hmm — the row with the cursor on the focused row: does the screen text show inverse video? screenText strips ANSI; the cell content is '•'. Cursor cell wraps inverse-video escapes on raw wire only. On screen, the char is '•'. Fine.

11. One more: RT4 `pasted` is `const` with `\n` — fine, plain literal.

12. `final pasted = 'k' * 200;` — runtime multiplication; comment says const_eval_type_num. Accurate fix per discussion.

13. **Doc-comment mentions**: AGENTS.md mentions line count? God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines. secret_sheet_residual_test.dart now ~470 lines. Fine.

14. Check analysis: `row.split('•').length - 1` for the password test? Not used there. OK.

15. RT4: `harness.sendText('\x1b[200~$pasted\x1b[201~')` — string interpolation with `$pasted` containing newlines — fine.

16. Potential issue in password_prompt test: secret length 15, `'•' * 15`. The sheet interior at 80 cols: password prompt frame — does the masked row fit 15 bullets? Yes.

17. **A subtle one in typeSecret copy (RT1)**: The doc comment claims "same [typeSecret] property anchor as secret_sheet_test.dart" — good cross-reference.

Now — is the RT4/RT5…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1287
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1287
- **Title**: gh-1257 [FLAKE] PTY integration: convert the 5 residual exact-bullet-count anchors (secret_sheet_residual_test / password_prompt_pty_test) to the gh-1244 property anchor
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1257-pty-bullet-anchors` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +149
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:28:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:54:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1257 (follow-up to gh-1244 / PR #1245 — reuses its established pattern verbatim, no second convention).

## Root Cause

Same flake class as gh-1244: five residual synchronization points pinned an exact transient bullet count on the raw stream (`waitForText('•••••')`). Under CI timing the PTY paints past the checkpoint before the 50 ms poll evaluates, and on the raw wire the focused secret row wraps the cursor cell in inverse-video escapes (`_secretValueSegmentRow` / `_cursorInputRow` in `lib/src/cli/tui_prompt.dart`), so N consecutive `•` need never exist in the stream at all. The feature was correct; the anchors were wrong. No production code changes.

## Fix (test-only, 2 files)

- `test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart`
  - RT1 (2 sites): the `waitForText('•••••')` checkpoints before each grant Enter replaced with the PR #1245 `typeSecret` property anchor (copied 1:1: `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + one re-anchor if `maskedValueRow` is null + race-free raw-transcript plaintext scan + frame-closed row bullet count == typed length).
  - RT4 (multiline paste): anchored on the painted screen's full first-segment run (`'•' * 19`); the masking property asserts the multiline shape `tui_prompt` actually renders — one bullet per pasted char, ONE FRAME ROW PER LINE (`[19, 6, 17]` over all `│`-closed masked rows) — plus the raw-transcript plaintext scan (`maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows; a single-row count can never see all 44 bullets).
  - RT5 (over-wide paste): `_wrapBodyLine` TRIMS an over-wide value row to the frame budget, so the full 200-bullet mask can never paint; anchored on a 40-bullet leading run (trimmed run is 75 cells at the 80-col PTY), asserting the frame-closed value row is all bullets (count >= 40, no `kk` anywhere on the anchored screen) + raw-transcript scan.
- `test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart`
  - The one `waitForText('•••••')` site converted to the same property anchor (`waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + `maskedValueRow` re-anchor + plaintext scans on the anchored screen); the pre-existing post-Enter raw checks unchanged.

AC1 verified statically: `grep -rn "waitForText('•••••')" test/` → no code hits remain (one doc-comment mention in the converted file explains the replaced anti-pattern).

## Relationship to PR #1284 (base secret_sheet_test quarantine)

#1284 quarantined `secret_sheet_test.dart` for the PTY **boot-timeout** signature (freeze-ledger 1st hit at secret_sheet_test.dart:194) — a different failure mode from this ticket's bullet-anchor class (same PTY integration family, different sig). This PR does not touch that file, the quarantine entry, or `pty_harness.dart` (hot zone — no harness changes were needed; `maskedValueRow` already on main covers all sites). Whether the #1284 quarantine can lift is independent of this lane.

## Test Coverage / Gate disclosure

- Local targeted gate `dart test test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart --tags integration` attempted ONCE on the fleet Mac box and **SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137)** — the known live-LLM-loop condition; no output faked, not retried. The hermetic `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` guard rules were verified by inspection instead (every `waitForScreen` captures its result; no unanchored screen reads in danger windows).
- **PR CI is the real gate**: the pty/nightly legs run both files; AC2 (repeated green runs of the PTY leg) is CI-side by construction — the anchors synchronize on stable painted-screen properties, so a raced checkpoint can no longer be missed.
- No timeouts raised beyond the 1245 precedent (30 s screen waits), no sleeps added.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call

blocks.text:
The typeSecret copy matches the precedent nearly verbatim. Now let me evaluate the actual review points.

Key areas to scrutinize:

1. **password_prompt_pty_test.dart**: the `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` for `secret = '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` (15 chars). Does the password prompt's masked row close with `│`? The test doesn't call maskedValueRow for the count assertion — it only uses it as a re-anchor check. Fine.

   However: one subtle issue — in the password prompt test, is the masked row frame-closed with `│`? Doesn't matter, it's only used for re-anchor.

2. **Race concern in RT4's multiline rows assertion**: `maskedRows` filters ALL rows that contain '•' and end with '│'. The first-segment run is 19 bullets; anchor is `'•' * 19`. Fine. But does any other frame row potentially contain bullets? E.g., the reason row or name row wouldn't contain bullets. OK.

   One issue: RT4 asserts exact list `[19, 6, 17]`. Is this over-pinning a rendering shape that could legitimately change? It's a masking property — pinned intentionally. Fine.

3. **RT5 anchor `'•' * 40`**: comment says the trimmed run is 75 cells at 80-col PTY. Wait — the anchor on a 40-bullet run: `waitForScreen` checks `screenText.contains('•' * 40)`. Could 40 consecutive bullets appear across a WRAPPED row? `expectFrameIntact` requires rows don't wrap. Also the bullet run could exist partially... it's monotone, fine.

   Hmm, one subtle problem in RT5: `maskedValueRow(screen)` gets the FIRST frame-closed bullet row. But the row at the anchor time might be an intermediate frame — e.g., bracketed paste updates arrive in chunks? `sendText` writes the entire paste at once, so one buffer update. The row bullets: 200 chars trimmed to 75 cells. Could the first frame show fewer than 75 bullets and the row is already frame-closed? The assertion is >= 40, robust to that. Good.

4. **RT4 raw-output check**: `harness.rawOutput.contains(pasted)` — the pasted contains newlines; raw output would carry `\r\n`? Bracketed paste with raw mode... the CLI's input handling wouldn't echo. The check that no `\r` survives is done on the transcript. If the terminal converts LF to CRLF in echo... not echoed anyway. Pre-existing pattern though (typeSecret does the same with `secret`). Fine.

5. **The RT4 maskedRows potential flake**: `.where((l) => l.contains('•') && l.trimRight().endsWith('│'))` — if the anchored frame catches a row before its closing border, that row is excluded from maskedRows, causing [19,6] vs [19,6,17] failure. But typeSecret precedent re-anchors once on null; RT4 does NOT re-anchor. The anchor `'•' * 19` exists only once the pasted frame painted... but frame rows could paint one at a time. The waitForScreen returns the first frame containing 19 bullets — that frame may not yet have all three rows closed. Hmm, actually if 19 bullets of row 1 are painted, rows below paint later. The bullet rows are painted presumably in one repaint (single buffer update), but the frame-closing border repaint may lag (as noted in typeSecret's re-anchor comment). If the value rows are painted before the frame's closing border, the `.endsWith('│')` filter would drop rows → maskedRows mismatch → flake. The typeSecret precedent explicitly tolerates "the anchored frame can still predate the value row's closing border by one repaint; re-anchor once". RT4 and RT5 don't do the re-anchor. RT5 does check via maskedValueRow and throws StateError if null (which would be a hard failure, not a re-anchor). Actually RT5: `final row = maskedValueRow(screen); if (row == null) throw StateError(...)` — same as typeSecret's post-re-anchor behavior. But RT4 does no re-anchor at all before filtering.

   Is this a real flake risk? The PR claims the re-anchor concern applies where relevant. In RT4, the anchor is 19 bullets on the screen; when that paints, the frame is being drawn — each row individually ends with `│`. Does the masked value row end with `│` immediately when painted? The border column is painted as part of the frame; tui_prompt paints the whole frame per repaint presumably. In a single repaint, all rows close. The race window is between the 19-bullet row painting and the frame border painting — if they're separate repaint passes. typeSecret's re-anchor was added exactly because of this observed race (gh-1244 review thread). RT4/RT5 lack it. But waitForScreen returns at the first frame containing '•'*19; the frame content could be partially painted if dart_tui diffs and emits row by row... Actually the xterm emulator assembles the final screen; the "screen" at poll time is the current emulator state which may show a half-painted frame. Since waitForScreen polls every 50ms, and dart_tui emits whole frames quickly, the probability of catching a torn frame is low but nonzero — that's exactly why the re-anchor exists in the pattern this PR claims to copy "1:1". This is at most a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT consistency point: RT4 and RT5 skip the re-anchor that the copied pattern includes.

   Hmm, but the PR description says "the `maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows". It deliberately deviates. The risk: on a loaded CI runner, if the anchored frame predates a border, `maskedRows` would be `[19]` or `[19, 6]` etc. → test fails → new flake, the very thing this PR fixes. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (consistency with the established pattern; real flake-class risk), or SUGGESTION. Given the repo treats flake recurrence seriously, I'd say IMPORTANT.

6. **RT5 `screen.contains('kk')` check**: checks no two consecutive 'k' anywhere on the screen. Fine. But note: 'k' could appear in other legit screen text? Contains 'kk' — words with double-k unlikely. Fine.

7. **password test**: removed `expect(harness.screenText.contains(secret), isFalse)` replaced with anchored screen check. Slightly weaker (no longer checks the LIVE screen at that moment), but rawOutput covers everything and the anchored screen is asserted. Acceptable — documented. Also note reg-test: `waitForScreen` result captured — yes, `var screen = ...`. RT1 typeSecret captures. RT4/RT5 capture. Good.

8. **RT1 second site** (`second-secret`, 13 chars): `typeSecret` asserts row bullet count == 13. The history tool row `• request_secret · …` contains a single bullet, not frame-closed — filtered. But wait: the first secret was 's3cr3t-TOKEN-42' (15 chars). When typing the second secret, could the anchored screen still contain the FIRST sheet's row with 15 bullets and the second's with 13? The sheet fully replaced — first row gone (RT1 asserts no '•••' before). maskedValueRow takes the FIRST matching row; if a ghost of the old row lingered, count would be 15 ≠ 13 → fail loudly. That's a correct assertion.

9. **Timeout raise**: from 10s to 30s — consistent with 1245 precedent. Fine.

10. **RT4 maskedRows includes rows beyond the sheet?** The value field's masked rows end with '│'. Any other row on screen containing '•' and ending with '│'? The secret sheet frame's other rows (name, reason) don't contain bullets. OK. But hmm — the row with the cursor on the focused row: does the screen text show inverse video? screenText strips ANSI; the cell content is '•'. Cursor cell wraps inverse-video escapes on raw wire only. On screen, the char is '•'. Fine.

11. One more: RT4 `pasted` is `const` with `\n` — fine, plain literal.

12. `final pasted = 'k' * 200;` — runtime multiplication; comment says const_eval_type_num. Accurate fix per discussion.

13. **Doc-comment mentions**: AGENTS.md mentions line count? God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines. secret_sheet_residual_test.dart now ~470 lines. Fine.

14. Check analysis: `row.split('•').length - 1` for the password test? Not used there. OK.

15. RT4: `harness.sendText('\x1b[200~$pasted\x1b[201~')` — string interpolation with `$pasted` containing newlines — fine.

16. Potential issue in password_prompt test: secret length 15, `'•' * 15`. The sheet interior at 80 cols: password prompt frame — does the masked row fit 15 bullets? Yes.

17. **A subtle one in typeSecret copy (RT1)**: The doc comment claims "same [typeSecret] property anchor as secret_sheet_test.dart" — good cross-reference.

Now — is the RT4/RT5…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1287
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1287
- **Title**: gh-1257 [FLAKE] PTY integration: convert the 5 residual exact-bullet-count anchors (secret_sheet_residual_test / password_prompt_pty_test) to the gh-1244 property anchor
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1257-pty-bullet-anchors` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +149
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:28:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:54:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1257 (follow-up to gh-1244 / PR #1245 — reuses its established pattern verbatim, no second convention).

## Root Cause

Same flake class as gh-1244: five residual synchronization points pinned an exact transient bullet count on the raw stream (`waitForText('•••••')`). Under CI timing the PTY paints past the checkpoint before the 50 ms poll evaluates, and on the raw wire the focused secret row wraps the cursor cell in inverse-video escapes (`_secretValueSegmentRow` / `_cursorInputRow` in `lib/src/cli/tui_prompt.dart`), so N consecutive `•` need never exist in the stream at all. The feature was correct; the anchors were wrong. No production code changes.

## Fix (test-only, 2 files)

- `test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart`
  - RT1 (2 sites): the `waitForText('•••••')` checkpoints before each grant Enter replaced with the PR #1245 `typeSecret` property anchor (copied 1:1: `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + one re-anchor if `maskedValueRow` is null + race-free raw-transcript plaintext scan + frame-closed row bullet count == typed length).
  - RT4 (multiline paste): anchored on the painted screen's full first-segment run (`'•' * 19`); the masking property asserts the multiline shape `tui_prompt` actually renders — one bullet per pasted char, ONE FRAME ROW PER LINE (`[19, 6, 17]` over all `│`-closed masked rows) — plus the raw-transcript plaintext scan (`maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows; a single-row count can never see all 44 bullets).
  - RT5 (over-wide paste): `_wrapBodyLine` TRIMS an over-wide value row to the frame budget, so the full 200-bullet mask can never paint; anchored on a 40-bullet leading run (trimmed run is 75 cells at the 80-col PTY), asserting the frame-closed value row is all bullets (count >= 40, no `kk` anywhere on the anchored screen) + raw-transcript scan.
- `test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart`
  - The one `waitForText('•••••')` site converted to the same property anchor (`waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + `maskedValueRow` re-anchor + plaintext scans on the anchored screen); the pre-existing post-Enter raw checks unchanged.

AC1 verified statically: `grep -rn "waitForText('•••••')" test/` → no code hits remain (one doc-comment mention in the converted file explains the replaced anti-pattern).

## Relationship to PR #1284 (base secret_sheet_test quarantine)

#1284 quarantined `secret_sheet_test.dart` for the PTY **boot-timeout** signature (freeze-ledger 1st hit at secret_sheet_test.dart:194) — a different failure mode from this ticket's bullet-anchor class (same PTY integration family, different sig). This PR does not touch that file, the quarantine entry, or `pty_harness.dart` (hot zone — no harness changes were needed; `maskedValueRow` already on main covers all sites). Whether the #1284 quarantine can lift is independent of this lane.

## Test Coverage / Gate disclosure

- Local targeted gate `dart test test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart --tags integration` attempted ONCE on the fleet Mac box and **SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137)** — the known live-LLM-loop condition; no output faked, not retried. The hermetic `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` guard rules were verified by inspection instead (every `waitForScreen` captures its result; no unanchored screen reads in danger windows).
- **PR CI is the real gate**: the pty/nightly legs run both files; AC2 (repeated green runs of the PTY leg) is CI-side by construction — the anchors synchronize on stable painted-screen properties, so a raced checkpoint can no longer be missed.
- No timeouts raised beyond the 1245 precedent (30 s screen waits), no sleeps added.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`

The typeSecret copy matches the precedent nearly verbatim. Now let me evaluate the actual review points.

Key areas to scrutinize:

1. **password_prompt_pty_test.dart**: the `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` for `secret = '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` (15 chars). Does the password prompt's masked row close with `│`? The test doesn't call maskedValueRow for the count assertion — it only uses it as a re-anchor check. Fine.

   However: one subtle issue — in the password prompt test, is the masked row frame-closed with `│`? Doesn't matter, it's only used for re-anchor.

2. **Race concern in RT4's multiline rows assertion**: `maskedRows` filters ALL rows that contain '•' and end with '│'. The first-segment run is 19 bullets; anchor is `'•' * 19`. Fine. But does any other frame row potentially contain bullets? E.g., the reason row or name row wouldn't contain bullets. OK.

   One issue: RT4 asserts exact list `[19, 6, 17]`. Is this over-pinning a rendering shape that could legitimately change? It's a masking property — pinned intentionally. Fine.

3. **RT5 anchor `'•' * 40`**: comment says the trimmed run is 75 cells at 80-col PTY. Wait — the anchor on a 40-bullet run: `waitForScreen` checks `screenText.contains('•' * 40)`. Could 40 consecutive bullets appear across a WRAPPED row? `expectFrameIntact` requires rows don't wrap. Also the bullet run could exist partially... it's monotone, fine.

   Hmm, one subtle problem in RT5: `maskedValueRow(screen)` gets the FIRST frame-closed bullet row. But the row at the anchor time might be an intermediate frame — e.g., bracketed paste updates arrive in chunks? `sendText` writes the entire paste at once, so one buffer update. The row bullets: 200 chars trimmed to 75 cells. Could the first frame show fewer than 75 bullets and the row is already frame-closed? The assertion is >= 40, robust to that. Good.

4. **RT4 raw-output check**: `harness.rawOutput.contains(pasted)` — the pasted contains newlines; raw output would carry `\r\n`? Bracketed paste with raw mode... the CLI's input handling wouldn't echo. The check that no `\r` survives is done on the transcript. If the terminal converts LF to CRLF in echo... not echoed anyway. Pre-existing pattern though (typeSecret does the same with `secret`). Fine.

5. **The RT4 maskedRows potential flake**: `.where((l) => l.contains('•') && l.trimRight().endsWith('│'))` — if the anchored frame catches a row before its closing border, that row is excluded from maskedRows, causing [19,6] vs [19,6,17] failure. But typeSecret precedent re-anchors once on null; RT4 does NOT re-anchor. The anchor `'•' * 19` exists only once the pasted frame painted... but frame rows could paint one at a time. The waitForScreen returns the first frame containing 19 bullets — that frame may not yet have all three rows closed. Hmm, actually if 19 bullets of row 1 are painted, rows below paint later. The bullet rows are painted presumably in one repaint (single buffer update), but the frame-closing border repaint may lag (as noted in typeSecret's re-anchor comment). If the value rows are painted before the frame's closing border, the `.endsWith('│')` filter would drop rows → maskedRows mismatch → flake. The typeSecret precedent explicitly tolerates "the anchored frame can still predate the value row's closing border by one repaint; re-anchor once". RT4 and RT5 don't do the re-anchor. RT5 does check via maskedValueRow and throws StateError if null (which would be a hard failure, not a re-anchor). Actually RT5: `final row = maskedValueRow(screen); if (row == null) throw StateError(...)` — same as typeSecret's post-re-anchor behavior. But RT4 does no re-anchor at all before filtering.

   Is this a real flake risk? The PR claims the re-anchor concern applies where relevant. In RT4, the anchor is 19 bullets on the screen; when that paints, the frame is being drawn — each row individually ends with `│`. Does the masked value row end with `│` immediately when painted? The border column is painted as part of the frame; tui_prompt paints the whole frame per repaint presumably. In a single repaint, all rows close. The race window is between the 19-bullet row painting and the frame border painting — if they're separate repaint passes. typeSecret's re-anchor was added exactly because of this observed race (gh-1244 review thread). RT4/RT5 lack it. But waitForScreen returns at the first frame containing '•'*19; the frame content could be partially painted if dart_tui diffs and emits row by row... Actually the xterm emulator assembles the final screen; the "screen" at poll time is the current emulator state which may show a half-painted frame. Since waitForScreen polls every 50ms, and dart_tui emits whole frames quickly, the probability of catching a torn frame is low but nonzero — that's exactly why the re-anchor exists in the pattern this PR claims to copy "1:1". This is at most a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT consistency point: RT4 and RT5 skip the re-anchor that the copied pattern includes.

   Hmm, but the PR description says "the `maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows". It deliberately deviates. The risk: on a loaded CI runner, if the anchored frame predates a border, `maskedRows` would be `[19]` or `[19, 6]` etc. → test fails → new flake, the very thing this PR fixes. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (consistency with the established pattern; real flake-class risk), or SUGGESTION. Given the repo treats flake recurrence seriously, I'd say IMPORTANT.

6. **RT5 `screen.contains('kk')` check**: checks no two consecutive 'k' anywhere on the screen. Fine. But note: 'k' could appear in other legit screen text? Contains 'kk' — words with double-k unlikely. Fine.

7. **password test**: removed `expect(harness.screenText.contains(secret), isFalse)` replaced with anchored screen check. Slightly weaker (no longer checks the LIVE screen at that moment), but rawOutput covers everything and the anchored screen is asserted. Acceptable — documented. Also note reg-test: `waitForScreen` result captured — yes, `var screen = ...`. RT1 typeSecret captures. RT4/RT5 capture. Good.

8. **RT1 second site** (`second-secret`, 13 chars): `typeSecret` asserts row bullet count == 13. The history tool row `• request_secret · …` contains a single bullet, not frame-closed — filtered. But wait: the first secret was 's3cr3t-TOKEN-42' (15 chars). When typing the second secret, could the anchored screen still contain the FIRST sheet's row with 15 bullets and the second's with 13? The sheet fully replaced — first row gone (RT1 asserts no '•••' before). maskedValueRow takes the FIRST matching row; if a ghost of the old row lingered, count would be 15 ≠ 13 → fail loudly. That's a correct assertion.

9. **Timeout raise**: from 10s to 30s — consistent with 1245 precedent. Fine.

10. **RT4 maskedRows includes rows beyond the sheet?** The value field's masked rows end with '│'. Any other row on screen containing '•' and ending with '│'? The secret sheet frame's other rows (name, reason) don't contain bullets. OK. But hmm — the row with the cursor on the focused row: does the screen text show inverse video? screenText strips ANSI; the cell content is '•'. Cursor cell wraps inverse-video escapes on raw wire only. On screen, the char is '•'. Fine.

11. One more: RT4 `pasted` is `const` with `\n` — fine, plain literal.

12. `final pasted = 'k' * 200;` — runtime multiplication; comment says const_eval_type_num. Accurate fix per discussion.

13. **Doc-comment mentions**: AGENTS.md mentions line count? God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines. secret_sheet_residual_test.dart now ~470 lines. Fine.

14. Check analysis: `row.split('•').length - 1` for the password test? Not used there. OK.

15. RT4: `harness.sendText('\x1b[200~$pasted\x1b[201~')` — string interpolation with `$pasted` containing newlines — fine.

16. Potential issue in password_prompt test: secret length 15, `'•' * 15`. The sheet interior at 80 cols: password prompt frame — does the masked row fit 15 bullets? Yes.

17. **A subtle one in typeSecret copy (RT1)**: The doc comment claims "same [typeSecret] property anchor as secret_sheet_test.dart" — good cross-reference.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1287
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1287
- **Title**: gh-1257 [FLAKE] PTY integration: convert the 5 residual exact-bullet-count anchors (secret_sheet_residual_test / password_prompt_pty_test) to the gh-1244 property anchor
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1257-pty-bullet-anchors` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +149
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:28:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:54:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1257 (follow-up to gh-1244 / PR #1245 — reuses its established pattern verbatim, no second convention).

## Root Cause

Same flake class as gh-1244: five residual synchronization points pinned an exact transient bullet count on the raw stream (`waitForText('•••••')`). Under CI timing the PTY paints past the checkpoint before the 50 ms poll evaluates, and on the raw wire the focused secret row wraps the cursor cell in inverse-video escapes (`_secretValueSegmentRow` / `_cursorInputRow` in `lib/src/cli/tui_prompt.dart`), so N consecutive `•` need never exist in the stream at all. The feature was correct; the anchors were wrong. No production code changes.

## Fix (test-only, 2 files)

- `test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart`
  - RT1 (2 sites): the `waitForText('•••••')` checkpoints before each grant Enter replaced with the PR #1245 `typeSecret` property anchor (copied 1:1: `waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + one re-anchor if `maskedValueRow` is null + race-free raw-transcript plaintext scan + frame-closed row bullet count == typed length).
  - RT4 (multiline paste): anchored on the painted screen's full first-segment run (`'•' * 19`); the masking property asserts the multiline shape `tui_prompt` actually renders — one bullet per pasted char, ONE FRAME ROW PER LINE (`[19, 6, 17]` over all `│`-closed masked rows) — plus the raw-transcript plaintext scan (`maskedValueRow`'s guard generalized to all rows; a single-row count can never see all 44 bullets).
  - RT5 (over-wide paste): `_wrapBodyLine` TRIMS an over-wide value row to the frame budget, so the full 200-bullet mask can never paint; anchored on a 40-bullet leading run (trimmed run is 75 cells at the 80-col PTY), asserting the frame-closed value row is all bullets (count >= 40, no `kk` anywhere on the anchored screen) + raw-transcript scan.
- `test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart`
  - The one `waitForText('•••••')` site converted to the same property anchor (`waitForScreen('•' * secret.length)` + `maskedValueRow` re-anchor + plaintext scans on the anchored screen); the pre-existing post-Enter raw checks unchanged.

AC1 verified statically: `grep -rn "waitForText('•••••')" test/` → no code hits remain (one doc-comment mention in the converted file explains the replaced anti-pattern).

## Relationship to PR #1284 (base secret_sheet_test quarantine)

#1284 quarantined `secret_sheet_test.dart` for the PTY **boot-timeout** signature (freeze-ledger 1st hit at secret_sheet_test.dart:194) — a different failure mode from this ticket's bullet-anchor class (same PTY integration family, different sig). This PR does not touch that file, the quarantine entry, or `pty_harness.dart` (hot zone — no harness changes were needed; `maskedValueRow` already on main covers all sites). Whether the #1284 quarantine can lift is independent of this lane.

## Test Coverage / Gate disclosure

- Local targeted gate `dart test test/integration/secret_sheet_residual_test.dart test/integration/password_prompt_pty_test.dart --tags integration` attempted ONCE on the fleet Mac box and **SIGKILLed by the machine guard (exit 137)** — the known live-LLM-loop condition; no output faked, not retried. The hermetic `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` guard rules were verified by inspection instead (every `waitForScreen` captures its result; no unanchored screen reads in danger windows).
- **PR CI is the real gate**: the pty/nightly legs run both files; AC2 (repeated green runs of the PTY leg) is CI-side by construction — the anchors synchronize on stable painted-screen properties, so a raced checkpoint can no longer be missed.
- No timeouts raised beyond the 1245 precedent (30 s screen waits), no sleeps added.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…
